2.15.betting_forecast: 6/4 Laravie, 5/2 Balgowan, 8/1 In The Post, 10/1 Charles Morin, Regally Blonde, 12/1 Everest, Sapphire Sirocco, 33/1 Adrian,
2.15.spotlight_verdict: The most interesting runner is LARAVIE, who made a low-key start to her Flat career last month but, if judged on last year's hurdling form, could be on a very good mark for this handicap debut. She's very likely to be suited by today's step up in trip and the refitted visor (worn for all four hurdle wins) further enhances her appeal. Balgowan might have been unlucky not to win over C&D last month but he's rather frustrating. In The Post, completely unexposed over this sort of trip, is feared more.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Returns from break on career-low mark but this regressive 9yo is yet to add to his German Group 3 success in 2021 and is difficult to enthuse over.

Has modest 1-28 strike-rate (includes five hurdle runs) but was denied a clear run before finishing well for close third over C&D last month and gets another chance off the same mark today; respected.
Yet to add to his 1m1f turf win here in 2024 but went close over 1m4f here (AW) in February and also ran well when fifth (just behind Balgowan) over C&D last month; probably won't be far away.
Flat and dual hurdle winner during busy summer for James Owen last year but well beaten (over hurdles) on stable debut on Tuesday and returns to the Flat with quite a bit to prove.

Finished well for narrow win in 1m4f classified here last month, opening her account on 15th start under all codes; soundly beaten in Wolverhampton handicap over that trip since but could plausibly have untapped potential over 2m on the Flat.
horses.breeding: b m Kayf Tara - Sudden Wish

horses.spotlight_comment: Low-mileage 4yo; safely held in first three handicaps (1m-1m2f) but this big hike up in trip is an interesting move; cheekpieces removed after one use; well worth a glance in the bettting.

Developed into fairly useful hurdler when fitted with a visor last year, winning four times (2m4f-2m7f); didn't show a great deal in three AW novice races (8.6f-1m3f) in March but this longer trip ought to suit much better and she has the visor refitted on her Flat handicap debut; must be considered.
horses.breeding: b m Sans Frontieres - Lohort Castle

horses.spotlight_comment: Dual turf winner (1m6f/2m) last summer; off since two below-par runs in the autumn, though, and still on fairly tough mark for this rare AW run.

Scored over C&D off basement mark for Pat Phelan in November; changed hands for 4,400gns after disappointing C&D run in January and makes stable debut after 110-day break but still worth a market check.
horses.breeding: gr g Reliable Man - Anna Desta

horses.spotlight_comment: Yet to add to his 1m1f turf win here in 2024 but went close over 1m4f here (AW) in February and also ran well when fifth (just behind Balgowan) over C&D last month; probably won't be far away.

2.45.betting_forecast: 5/4 Travel Agent, 4/1 Lequinto, 5/1 Diamond Dreamer, Maharajas Express, 8/1 Mart.
2.45.spotlight_verdict: This can go to TRAVEL AGENT (nap), who looked in excellent nick at Wolverhampton ten days ago. Adam Kirby's 4yo is not yet fully exposed after only 12 runs, and his other win was gained over this C&D. Diamond Dreamer (second choice) is better than he showed last time and remains well handicapped, while Mart is also on a good mark.[Chris Wilson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Didn't fire at Chelmsford last time but was a close second off a reduced mark here (5f) two starts ago and this return to 6f won't be a problem; can make his presence felt.
horses.breeding: b g Oasis Dream - Diamond Blaise

horses.spotlight_comment: Into the veteran stage now and it's a long time since his latest AW win but he made the frame over C&D two starts ago and kept on well for second behind a next-time-out winner at Wolverhampton (6f) on his most recent outing.
horses.breeding: b g No Nay Never - Flower Fashion

horses.spotlight_comment: Won three times over 5f on AW/turf last year; stays 6f perfectly well and can easily be excused his defeat on heavy ground in September but has fitness to prove after a seven-month break.
Gained two of his seven wins over this C&D; below form lately but endured a wide trip when last in action and is now 3lb lower than when a close second over C&D in January.

Came good for new stable at third attempt, overcoming some traffic issues before winning readily at Wolverhampton (6f) ten days ago; 4lb rise does not look excessive and this C&D also suits; good chance.

3.15.betting_forecast: 5/4 Ticker Tape, 5/1 Lady Magu, Madrisa, 6/1 St Hilda, 7/1 Barbuda Bay, 12/1 Spinney, 20/1 Neswick, 33/1 Last Flight, Love
3.15.spotlight_verdict: A half-sister to a few useful winners for the Gosden yard, notably Courage Mon Ami, today's longer trip will suit TICKER TAPE and she looks the one most likely among those with experience. Newcomers Lady Magu and Madrisa wouldn't need to be anything out of the ordinary though.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Not gone on from last August's debut second here, falling well below market expectations on her comeback three weeks ago; said to have raced freely that day, upped to 1m, and will need to settle going further again.
Yard made a bright start but this filly offered little in two runs early last summer, pulling hard and finishing tailed off each time; low-grade handicaps are probably next up.
Huge prices for two 1m Kempton novices earlier in the year and ran as expected each time.
30,000gns yearling who's the third foal of a maiden and a sister to an ordinary Irish hurdler; been found a weak-looking maiden on debut and the market will guide.
Not persevered with once her chance had gone in an ordinary fillies' novice at Newcastle late last year; drawn widest as she returns from four months off and goes up in trip.
Dam won over 2m on Tapeta (0-65 handicap) for the yard; easy to back, finished well held on her 1m debut five weeks ago and may well be one for handicaps down the line.
First foal of an unraced half-sister to dual 1m2f Group 3 winner Extra Elusive and the yard's Group 2 Gimcrack winner Ajaya; blinkers go straight on for a stable yet to hit top gear for the season.
Seventh foal of a dual Tapeta winner over further; trainer, who also runs St Hilda, doesn't have the best of records with 3yos on the AW in recent times.
Dam useful at around this trip but she's produced nothing of note and this filly went for just 1,000gns as a yearling; perhaps best watched unless there's good money for her.
Needed the experience from a wide stall when shaping fairly on her 7f debut here last November (some way off the front three); entitled to improve and her dam won her maiden at around this trip.

Very well related and today's longer trip is likely to suit on pedigree, with a steadily run 8.6f never going to prove optimal on her Wolverhampton debut late last month; will only have learned from that.
Pulled hard when tailed off in a bumper in February and again over 1m round Kempton early in the month; can't be backed.

3.45.betting_forecast: 5/4 El Matador, 5/1 Silver Trumpet, 6/1 Freddie's Star, Port Road, 8/1 Tiger Crusade, 12/1 King's Vanity, 16/1 Lunario.
3.45.spotlight_verdict: The well-related EL MATADOR didn't get the breaks in some good-class handicaps late last summer and has much the most potential of these, having since been gelded. Silver Trumpet will be happier back down from 1m and rates the main danger.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won two novices over this trip last May before finishing held in some decent-quality handicaps (among the favourites each time); not fully exposed as yet and this is a deal less competitive on his AW debut, back from seven months off, having been gelded.
horses.breeding: ch g Lope De Vega - Bulrushes

horses.spotlight_comment: Chelmsford win at long odds-on last November didn't amount to much and he's perhaps best judged on his subsequent handicap debut, when never involved; needs to improve a deal on that back from five months off.

Only seen once since leaving Andrew Balding 18 months ago, when well held last October; won his novice over C&D and the hood going back on should help but it's hard to know whether he's still up to this sort of mark.

Last four wins have come in high summer, including two from the front last year for Jack Dace (rides Tiger Crusade), and he remains weighted to his best; didn't offer much on his comeback three weeks ago and an easy 7f is a bare minimum these days.
Wins both came off a 3lb lower mark over 1m round Kempton, latterly in January; there's nothing to suggest he's best caught fresh, so he looks to have a bit to overcome back from three months off.

Found 1m stretching him on his comeback from five months off and is entitled to improve, back in the cheekpieces last sported last July; still paying the price for his easy Epsom win last August, though, and there's not much wiggle room off this mark.

Consistent record round here (2-4 over C&D) and is back on the mark off which he won here in January; not in the same form of late, there's always a chance he'll blow the start and it's no certainty the race will be set up for him.
horses.breeding: b g No Nay Never - Folle Allure

4.15.betting_forecast: 9/4 Gladiadora, 6/1 Dayman, Francisco, 7/1 Twirler, 8/1 Bint Havana Gold, Cooramook, 10/1 Vitalline, 16/1 Twitch, 20/1 Miss
4.15.spotlight_verdict: This is far from overloaded with pace and looks a minefield, with a good few characters on show. Another furlong would have perhaps been optimal for GLADIADORA but she arrives at the top of her game and still looks the safest option. Cooramook, who's gone well round here before, is another to consider.[Graham Wheldon]

horses.spotlight_comment: Dual 7f winner early last year but has done a lot of recent racing in sprints and she pulled hard back up to this trip last month; a danger that she'll do the same again from the outside stall and much will hinge on how she settles early.
horses.breeding: gr m Havana Gold - Wings Ablaze

horses.spotlight_comment: Remains a maiden and has had plenty of chances but she went close a couple of times round here for Harry Eustace; better effort at a big price last time, switched from cheekpieces to blinkers, and holds claims on that.
Regressive gelding who's often been inclined to pull hard since returning from a year off; winless since his 3yo days and there are safer options.

Often misses the break and can pull hard, so will always come with risks attached; has resumed in good form, though, latterly behind a couple of subsequent winners at Chelmsford, and is quite capable off this mark if things fall his way.

Has done most racing over further and an easy 7f is a bare minimum but she's returned from a short break with two solid efforts under Liam Wright; up another 2lb for her Nottingham near-miss but has to enter calculations.
Won three over 1m at Brighton last summer, latterly off a 1lb lower mark, before losing her way; a poor comeback effort for her new yard four weeks ago leaves her hard to recommend.
Wildly inconsistent mare whose C&D dead-heat in February (third course win) came from out of the blue at 33-1; reverted to type since and it's hard to know what to expect as always.

Goes well round switchback tracks and is back down in class today having contested a couple of 0-70 handicaps over C&D latterly; not much room for manoeuvre off this mark but is capable of running well.
horses.breeding: b m Cable Bay - Run Of The Day

horses.spotlight_comment: On the downgrade last year; third to Vitalline in a 0-50 classified event on his Kempton comeback early last month but has since run only fairly from the front over C&D; others appeal more.
String of poor efforts for two yards last year and two more this spring, latterly over C&D; this is easier again, dropped another 5lb in second-time cheekpieces, but he's hard to make a case for.
Serial slow starter who switches back from blinkers to the visor sported for last month's 0-50 Kempton win; will be happier back up from 6f but is yet another who'll need some luck from a wide stall.
horses.breeding: b g Due Diligence - Vitta's Touch

4.45.betting_forecast: 3/1 Caviar Cowboy, Storm Point, 6/1 Tactical Blitz, 7/1 Mighty Vega, 10/1 King Of Chaos, 12/1 If I Could Dream, Kilkenny Warrior,
4.45.spotlight_verdict: A few of these bring potential, not least CAVIAR COWBOY, who shaped really well when runner-up over 6f here last time (winner gone in again) and can go one better on his first venture into handicaps. Recent Kempton scorer Storm Point also has better days ahead of him and rates a big threat, while Mighty Vega, Pretty Ambitious and Robert Anstruther all need considering too.[Peter Entwistle]

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive colt who posted a very good second in 6f novice here last month, finishing well having conceded first run to the winner (gone in again since); looks to have more to offer now handicapping back up in trip; big shout.
Showed fair form in four runs at 2yrs, signing off with a good fourth in 7f Epsom nursery in September; since gelded and can't be discounted on his seasonal return.
horses.breeding: b g Havana Grey - Abundant Moon

horses.spotlight_comment: Proved consistent as a 2yo without winning, signing off with a solid 7f nursery third at Haydock in October; off six months ahead of her Polytrack debut.
horses.breeding: b f Oasis Dream - Fleet Street

horses.spotlight_comment: Ended 2025 with nursery wins at Southwell (6f) and Lingfield (7f); shaped as if the run was needed after five months off when seventh at Kempton (7f) last month and can get back on track here.
Got off the mark in a C&D maiden in February but has failed to kick on back handicapping, though not totally disgraced when fifth at Beverley (7.5f) 12 days ago; needs to step forward.
In good form for his current yard, scoring over C&D in March and runner-up back over C&D 13 days ago; well in the mix despite a 2lb rise.
horses.breeding: b g Lucky Vega - Own Gift

horses.spotlight_comment: Runner-up in a pair of novices at Doncaster (7f) and Chelmsford (1m) before beating just one home in 7f Chelmsford maiden on her final run for Alice Haynes; it would come as no surprise to see this Wootton Bassett filly bounce back on yard/handicap debut.
horses.breeding: b f Wootton Bassett - Pretty Fair

horses.spotlight_comment: Failed to build on earlier promise when seventh on his handicap debut at Newbury (7f) in September; since gelded and could still do better on his seasonal return with his yard going well.
Fair juvenile maiden; gelded/off five months and not disgraced given he went freely when eighth of 12 in 6f handicap at Southwell 20 days ago; needs to build on it.

Off four months/gelded before taking a major step forward on his handicap debut when scoring at Kempton (7f) 26 days ago; up 4lb but the runner-up has gone in since; merits serious consideration with better still to come.
Made a winning start in handicaps at Newcastle (6f) in March; backed it up with a solid third of seven at Wolverhampton (7f; cheekpieces first time) 17 days ago; not out of things.

5.20.betting_forecast: 3/1 Son Of Man, Wonder, 5/1 Adjuvant, Way Of Life, 7/1 Skibo, 8/1 Metallo, 16/1 Rogue Impact, 25/1 Youthful King.
5.20.spotlight_verdict: Son Of Man and Wonder fought out a good finish over C&D last time and seem sure to go well again, while in-form C&D scorer Way Of Life (second choice) is also firmly in the picture. But the vote goes to SKIBO, who made a promising start to life in handicaps when twice placed at Salisbury and appeals as the type to do better, with few miles on the clock and the step up in trip a plus.[Peter Entwistle]

horses.spotlight_comment: Winless since May 2023 but he reappeared from five months off the track with a good third of five in 2m Southwell handicap 18 days ago; not out of things on his Polytrack debut eased 1lb.
On a long losing run but he comes here in decent form for his current yard, sixth of 14 in 1m2f handicap here 24 days ago; possibilities on his first go at this trip.
horses.breeding: b g Caravaggio - Sweet Dreams Baby

horses.spotlight_comment: Sole victory came over C&D but he has failed to beat a rival on his last two runs, gelded before coming in last of 9 at Kempton (1m4f) on his return three weeks ago; hard to warm to.
horses.breeding: b g Study Of Man - Just So

horses.spotlight_comment: Shaped well when placed in a pair of 1m2f Salisbury handicaps last summer; off eight months but this low-mileage son of New Approach should have more to offer in 2026, especially over 1m4f; interesting.
Gained a first success (since his debut in 2023) when edging out Wonder by 1l in 15-runner handicap over C&D 24 days ago; 2lb worse off here but still not taken lightly.
Kickstarted 2026 with success at Wolverhampton (9.5f) in March and backed it up with a good third of 12 in another 9.5f handicap there since; this C&D scorer can go well again off the same mark.

Thriving since the cheekpieces went on, scoring at Southwell (1m4f) in February and bettering that form when beaten 1l by Son Of Man over C&D 24 days ago; enjoys a 2lb weights pull now so he's a likely player.
C&D winner but he ended 2025 below par and beat one on his return from six months off in 1m4f Kempton handicap three weeks ago; needs to take a major step forward.
horses.breeding: b g Fountain Of Youth - Lady Moscou
